 Kolmar Korea is taking a broader role in promoting Korean beauty products overseas, helping six client brands reach potential buyers in Australia as demand for K-beauty continues to grow.
 The company said Sunday that it participated in the 2026 Korea Brand & Entertainment Expo in Melbourne from Nov. 5 to 7 alongside six client companies, holding approximately 150 export consultations with an estimated value of 6.8 billion won.
 The consultations accounted for more than 10 percent of all business consultations at the expo, which brought together around 110 participating companies.
 A local visitor listens to a product explanation at Kolmar Korea's booth during the Korea Brand & Entertainment Expo in Melbourne, Australia, held from Nov. 5 to 7. (Courtesy of Kolmar Korea) 
 Kolmar Korea's efforts come as Korean skincare products gain ground in Australia. According to the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA), Australia's imports of Korean skincare products rose 42.1 percent year-on-year to $147.7 million in 2025, making Korea the country's second-largest supplier after overtaking France.
 In the first half of 2026, Korean skincare products accounted for 19.5 percent of Australia's import market, just 1.6 percentage points behind the U.S., the largest supplier.
 The six participating clients were Goodai Global (Round Lab), PAKET (Mixsoon), MerciCo (Hwaroom), iUNIK (iUNIK), Gibest (Nine Tails) and HK inno.N (Be Wants).
 At the expo, Kolmar Korea showcased sunscreens, essences, creams and facial masks, along with demonstrations of the ultraviolet protection performance of sunscreens manufactured by the company. Visitors could also test five sun-care products.
 The company estimated that around 15,000 people visited its booth during the two-day consumer exhibition, which attracted approximately 30,000 visitors overall.
 Kolmar Korea officials hold business consultations with overseas buyers during the Korea Brand & Entertainment Expo in Melbourne, Australia, held from Nov. 5 to 7. (Courtesy of Kolmar Korea) 
 The event was organized by Korea's Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources and the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency.
 "Through this expo, we were able to introduce the competitiveness of K-beauty products directly to local buyers and consumers alongside our clients," a Kolmar Korea official said.
 "Having confirmed interest in the Australian market, we will continue supporting our clients in expanding local distribution channels and entering global markets," the official added.
